{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against 18 playbook rules. The package is unusually favourable to us: 16 of 18 rules are compliant, and several clauses (indemnification, IP and deliverable ownership, licence scope, assignment, transition assistance, insurance) sit at or above our preferred position. Two items require attention.

1. **Clause 7.7 (Customer-payable liquidated damages) — deviation, critical.** The clause imposes liquidated damages on us at fifteen percent of annual Fees per week, triggered by a payment being ten days late. This compounds beyond the remaining contract value and is walk-away territory rather than a near-miss. There is no offsetting early-termination-fee bargain to preserve (§ 10 imposes no termination fee and § 27 permits termination "without penalty"), so we propose deleting the mechanic outright and substituting an unconditional no-liquidated-damages statement. Vendor keeps its § 7.3 and general remedies for genuine non-payment.

2. **§ 21.1 (liability cap basis) — needs review, critical; verification did not pass.** The cap is properly mutual, the consequential-damages exclusion applies to "neither Party", and the Excluded Claims definition already carves out indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. The concern is the cap *basis*: "Fees" is defined at §§ 1.5–1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, and § 21.1 confines the measure to the first Order Form, which renders the twelve-month formula illusory. The proposed fix is a single surgical edit resetting the basis to fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim, with a USD 1,000,000 floor. **This finding carries a failed verification flag and should be confirmed against the executed definitions and Order Form before we raise it with Vendor.** We deliberately leave § 21.3 alone: broadening its payment carve-out beyond "undisputed amounts for conforming Services" is a preferred-only refinement that would expand our own uncapped exposure.

No other rule fails its fallback. Minor sub-elements short of preferred wording are noted in the findings and are not being redlined.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES (cl. 7.7) | 15% of annual Fees per week for a payment 10 days late; walk-away territory. Redline: delete and replace with unconditional no-LD statement. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Needs review** (verification failed) | § 21 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY | Cap mutual and carve-outs adequate; "Fees" basis (§§ 1.5–1.6, first Order Form only) makes the 12-month formula illusory. Single edit to § 21.1 proposed; confirm before raising. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 INDEMNIFICATION | Preferred position met; indemnification is an Excluded Claim under § 21.3, so uncapped. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES | Present assignment of Deliverables; Customer Data and Customer IP retained. Payment condition and § 13.3 suspension right noted only. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL | Preferred: free Affiliate/M&A assignment for us; Vendor restricted; no Vendor rights on our change of control (24.4). |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE | Affiliates and contractors covered; perpetual, irrevocable paid-up licences; suspension only for uncured material breach. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 TERMINATION | Unconditional Customer right (9.4), 30 days' notice (§ 29.4), accrued Fees only plus pro-rata refund; no Vendor convenience right. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES (cl. 12.3) | No exclusivity on us; cl. 12.4 restraint runs against Vendor and benefits us. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES (cl. 12.3) | Express confirmation of no non-compete, field-of-use or territory restriction on us. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 WARRANTIES | At or above fallback; hosted software warranted for the subscription term. 90-day Deliverable period noted only. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN | Up to six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; 30-day data return; no fee-dispute withholding. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 TERM AND RENEWAL | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 AUDIT RIGHTS | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, Vendor-borne cost below a 5% underpayment, no direct system access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION | New York law; exclusive New York County courts; no arbitration. Escalation step noted only. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 12 CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES (cl. 12.3) | No MFN on us; § 7.6 best-pricing warranty runs in our favour. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 AGREEMENT STRUCTURE AND SCOPE (cl. 2.1) | No minimum quantity or purchase commitment; § 7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use charges. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES (cl. 12.3) | No no-hire or solicitation restriction on us. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 INSURANCE | Preferred limits met, including USD 5,000,000 cyber and privacy cover; certificates on request. |

---

## Walk-away items

- **Clause 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7).** Liquidated damages of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a payment ten days late compound beyond the remaining contract value. Our finding places this in walk-away territory. We require deletion; there is no fallback bargain to trade against.
- **§ 21.1 — cap basis (subject to verification).** With "Fees" defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee and the measure confined to the first Order Form, the cap falls below our walk-away line. The proposed reset to twelve months' fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms, with a USD 1,000,000 floor, meets every fallback element. Because verification on this finding did not pass, we should re-confirm the definitional read before treating it as a walk-away.

---

## Next steps

1. **Re-verify § 21.1.** Confirm the §§ 1.5–1.6 definition of "Fees" and the first-Order-Form limitation against the execution version and the Order Form schedule; the automated verification on this finding failed and we should not raise it until the read is confirmed.
2. **Issue two redlines only.** (a) Delete clause 7.7 and insert an unconditional statement that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties, preserving Vendor's § 7.3 and general remedies; (b) subject to step 1, the single § 21.1 edit resetting the cap to twelve months' fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms, with a USD 1,000,000 floor.
3. **Hold the line on § 21.3.** We will not seek to broaden the payment carve-out; doing so would expand our own uncapped exposure to disputed and non-conforming amounts.
4. **Record, do not negotiate, the noted minor points.** Deliverable ownership conditioned on payment, the § 13.3 suspension right, the 90-day Deliverable warranty, the "direct" competitor qualifier in § 24.2, the § 28.3 escalation step and the request-triggered data-return clock are noted for the file and are not being redlined.
5. **Confirm remaining rules closed.** The other 16 rules are compliant on the verified findings and require no further action before signature."}
